extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and institutions seeking NIDA/NIH grant funding, grant administrators, and prospective SBIR/STTR applicants
extracted.subtask_description: A landing/index page summarizing NIDA funding resources, policies, and program-specific guidance to help investigators prepare, submit, and manage grant and contract applications for substance use disorder research.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDA Funding Opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDA-supported funding opportunities and research priorities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview/index of specific funding announcements and priority areas for research addressing substance use disorders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trans-NIH Funding Opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding initiatives and programs across NIH Institutes, Centers, and Offices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links or pointers to cross-Institute NIH initiatives that may be relevant to applicants (e.g., multi-IC programs, collaborative funding opportunities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for Grants & Contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources for grant/contract preparation and post-award administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical tools and guidance for preparing applications and managing awards after funding (e.g., administrative requirements, reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Considerations for NIDA Funding Opportunities and Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for Funding Opportunities and Grant Awards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIDA-specific requirements or considerations that apply to their FOAs and awards (policy or programmatic notes applicants should follow).

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Policies & Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policies for research conduct, stewardship, and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level NIH-wide policy requirements that affect applications and award management (e.g., responsible conduct, conflict of interest, human subjects protections as implemented across NIH).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for research involving human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards and requirements specific to clinical studies (e.g., protections for participants, IRB, informed consent, clinical trial registration/reporting expectations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Technology Transfer (STTR) Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year, NIDA provides more than $45 million* in awards to small businesses through SBIR & STTR programs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information and guidance for small business applicants seeking NIDA SBIR/STTR funding, including program purpose and funding scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Sharing Policies and Associated Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and guidance regarding the sharing of data for NIH- and NIDA-funded studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations and requirements for data sharing plans, repositories, and compliance with NIH/NIDA data sharing policies for funded projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The peer review process as the mechanism for evaluating applications; implies criteria used by reviewers though detail is provided on linked pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Application Forms
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required forms and templates applicants must complete and submit as part of an application package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant & Contract Application Process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural steps for preparing, submitting, and tracking grant and contract applications (timelines, submission portals, administrative steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDA Notice of Special Interest (NOSI)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices highlighting specific scientific areas of interest where NIDA encourages or expects applications; may modify or focus review priorities for those topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARP Research Awards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Featured/targeted award mechanism (details available on linked page); included here as a specific program opportunity within NIDA funding offerings.
